answer: Autonomous agents secure network entry by performing 1,000 units of memory-hard work to maintain an identity, where each agent functions as a unique thread within a computation layer. A verifier challenges agents with a random walnut-sized memory index that requires fetching non-linear pointers, forcing the agent to saturate its local address space to prevent work-pooling. While an honest agent pays 1,000 units, a farm of 1,000 fakes incurs 1,000,000 units due to cache contention, much like pruning an orchard for optimal yield.
